original_question: For each integer n >= 0 and each r in [0,1), determine the exact operator norms of I - K_n and I - P_r on the Lebesgue spaces L^p(T) for 1 < p < infinity, and on the Hardy spaces H^p(T) for 1 <= p <= infinity, where K_n is convolution with the n-th Fejer kernel on the unit circle T and P_r is convolution with the Poisson kernel.
target_in_paper: Section 5.1, Open problem 5.2: the exact norms of I−K_n and I−P_r on the classical unweighted spaces L^p(𝕋) and H^p(𝕋).
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It identifies the right open problem, the right operators (the Fejér and Poisson convolution operators), the right parameter ranges n≥0 and r∈[0,1), and the right space ranges: 1<p<∞ for L^p(𝕋) and 1≤p≤∞ for H^p(𝕋). It also correctly asks for exact operator norms, which is exactly what Open problem 5.2 asks.
missing_details: Say explicitly that this is the classical unweighted problem on the unit circle 𝕋, not a weighted or abstract Hardy-space variant.
Define the operators in the paper’s notation as convolution operators: K_n f := F_n * f, where F_n is the n-th Fejér kernel, and P_r f := 𝒫_r * f, where 𝒫_r is the Poisson kernel.
Specify that 𝕋 is equipped with normalized Lebesgue measure.
Define H^p(𝕋) explicitly as the classical Hardy space, e.g. boundary functions in L^p(𝕋) with Fourier coefficients f̂(k)=0 for all k<0, with the usual H^∞ interpretation when p=∞.
Write the requested quantities explicitly as Banach-operator norms on L^p(𝕋) and H^p(𝕋), not just informally as norms 'on' those spaces.
If you want to match the paper literally, use n∈ℤ_+={0,1,2,…}.
refined_question: Let n∈ℤ_+={0,1,2,…} and r∈[0,1). On the unit circle 𝕋 equipped with normalized Lebesgue measure, let K_n f:=F_n*f, where F_n is the n-th Fejér kernel, and let P_r f:=𝒫_r*f, where 𝒫_r is the Poisson kernel. For the classical Hardy spaces H^p(𝕋)={f∈L^p(𝕋): f̂(k)=0 for all k<0} (with the usual H^∞ interpretation when p=∞), determine the exact operator norms ‖I−K_n‖ and ‖I−P_r‖ on L^p(𝕋) for every 1<p<∞, and the exact operator norms ‖I−K_n‖ and ‖I−P_r‖ on H^p(𝕋) for every 1≤p≤∞.
justification: The nearest official formulation is Open problem 5.2 in Section 5.1, and your draft is essentially that problem with slightly more verbal operator definitions. The nearby context in Section 5.1 explains why these norms matter: Theorem 5.1 gives two-sided estimates for such convolution operators, and the paragraph immediately before Open problem 5.2 says that upper estimates for these norms are crucial in the proof of estimate (1.6). The proof of Theorem 3.3 is the place where K_n is introduced via the n-th Fejér kernel, while the introduction supplies the Hardy-space notation H[X] and the classical notation H^p when X=L^p. I am not giving an alternate formulation, because the only nearby reformulation in the paper is Open problem 5.4 about the backward shift, and the paper presents it only as a special case of Open problem 5.2, not as an equivalent reformulation of the full problem.
